sections.html:
Lake Oswego is a city about 7 miles south of Portland, mostly in Clackamas County with small portions in Multnomah and Washington counties. Its center is Oswego Lake, a private lake of roughly 400 acres that the Clackamas people called Waluga, meaning wild swan.

As of December 2024 the city had 25 formally recognized neighborhood associations. A few of them are Birdshill, Forest Hills, Lake Grove, Lakewood, Old Town, Palisades, Waluga, Westlake and Westridge. Knowing your neighborhood name helps when you describe the house to a buyer.

sections.h2: How did iron and a railroad shape Lake Oswego?
sections.html:
Lake Oswego began as a company town for iron, and the railroad then turned it into a place Portlanders could reach in a short ride.

In 1867 the Oregon Iron Company built the first charcoal iron smelter on the Pacific coast, and in 1882 the Oregon Iron & Steel Company built the first of two furnaces. The company struggled for more than forty years. The Red Electric interurban line was electrified in 1914, and passenger service peaked in 1920 with 64 daily trains. Oswego was incorporated in 1910. In 1960 the town took in part of Lake Grove and adopted the name Lake Oswego, which brought the whole lake inside city limits. A residential building boom followed in the 1930s, and landowners marketed lots with the slogan "Live Where You Play," using the Lake Grove Swim Park as an outdoor sales office.

sections.h2: Who owns the lake, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
A private group called the Lake Oswego Corporation owns the lake bed, which it received in 1942 from the Oregon Iron and Steel Company, so lake access comes with a membership attached to the deed.

The corporation says more than 4,000 local households are shareholders or easement members. Annual assessments and license fees, paid only by residents with deeded access, fund safety patrols, water quality work, dredging, dam maintenance and a boat ramp and marina. The corporation does not post dollar amounts on its public About page, so ask for current figures in writing before you list or sell.

Public access has been argued in court. On August 1, 2019, the Oregon Supreme Court recognized a public right to enter the lake from public land, and in April 2024 a Clackamas County judge found that the city had overstepped by blocking access from the Millennium Plaza Park. These rulings are part of the story buyers hear, so a lakefront seller should read the latest news before describing exclusivity in any listing.

sections.h2: What does the Lake Oswego tree code require?
sections.html:
Lake Oswego requires a permit to remove a tree of at least 6 inches in diameter, and it asks for replacement trees in most cases.

Under city code section 55.02, the rules work like this:

  • A tree is a woody plant with a trunk of 6 inches or more, and a significant tree is a healthy, non-invasive tree over 15 inches, or the only tree left on a lot.
  • A simple Type I permit covers up to two trees of 15 inches or less per year on a residential lot with a single-family house, though it does not apply within the 25-foot Oswego Lake setback.
  • Most other removals need a Type II permit with a posted sign, a 14-day comment period and a tentative decision.
  • Replacement usually means one 1.5-inch deciduous tree or one 6-foot evergreen for each tree removed, and two for a significant tree.
  • Each unlawful removal is a separate civil violation, and a stump of eight caliper inches or more counts as prima facie evidence.

Lakefront owners also answer to the Lake Oswego Corporation, whose tree policy says a removal of 6 inches or more from corporation land needs a city permit and the corporation's signature on the application. If you have cleared trees recently, keep the paperwork, because a buyer's attorney may ask.

sections.h2: How many people live in Lake Oswego, and who are the owners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 39,722 residents as of July 1, 2025, down from 40,731 in the 2020 census.

A median age of 47.3 points to a long-established owner base, and sellers in that group often ask about estate steps and downsizing.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Lake Oswego?
sections.html:
The Lake Oswego School District is the largest employer inside the city, followed by a retirement community, a medical practice and several technology and mortgage firms.

The district serves about 7,000 students through two high schools, Lake Oswego and Lakeridge, two junior highs and six elementary schools. A portion of the city lies in Portland Public Schools. TriMet has run the local bus service since 1970.

sections.h2: How do Clackamas County property taxes work for a Lake Oswego owner?
sections.html:
Lake Oswego owners pay Clackamas County property tax, which in 2025 was levied by 130 taxing districts across 357 tax code areas.

That patchwork is why two houses with similar values can get different bills. The county said about 6.0 percent of properties paid tax on real market value in 2025, because Measure 50 limits the growth of assessed value for the rest. Statewide, assessed value can rise 3 percent a year at most. The county's single-family median real market value was $595,816 countywide, so check your own account on the county site for your parcel's numbers.

In 2025 the first payment date moved to November 17 because November 15 fell on a Saturday, and appeals were accepted through December 31. The county's lobby is in Oregon City at 150 Beavercreek Road, Suite 135. Tell your title company which bill is current so the proration at closing is correct.

sections.h2: What does the City of Lake Oswego offer residents?
sections.html:
Lake Oswego is run under a council-manager form, with a mayor and six at-large councilors serving four-year terms. City Hall moved into a new building in April 2021.

The city maintains about 600 acres of parks and open space, including George Rogers Park, Millennium Plaza Park and the Lake Oswego Golf Course. The Lake Oswego Recreation and Aquatics Center opened in 2025, and the Willamette Shore Trolley runs tourist rides on the old rail line. Amenities of this kind are part of what a buyer sees in a house here, so a short list of nearby parks and trails helps in any conversation about price.

sections.h2: What do Lake Oswego sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Sellers here often face a few situations that call for a clear plan.

  • Lake rights: confirming that shareholder or easement status transfers, and what the annual fees are.
  • Trees: permits and replacement rules can slow a pre-sale cleanup, and the code says a removal solely for views does not qualify under the Type II criteria.
  • Estates and downsizing: an older resident base brings these sales up often.
  • Tax proration: the closing statement splits the current tax year, so know which installments you have paid.

A cash sale does not remove any of these items, but it lets you pick a closing date and avoid repairs, staging and showings. Title will still check lake rights and record the deed, and you should still read every number on the closing statement before you sign.

faqs.q: What county is Lake Oswego in?
faqs.a: Lake Oswego is mostly in Clackamas County, with small parts in Multnomah and Washington counties. It lies about 7 miles south of Portland.

The Lake Oswego Corporation owns the lake bed, which it received in 1942. More than 4,000 households are shareholders or easement members, and those with deeded access pay annual assessments and license fees.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Lake Oswego?
faqs.a: Yes, for a tree of 6 inches in diameter or more. A Type I permit can cover up to two trees of 15 inches or less per year on a single-family residential lot, and most other removals need a Type II permit.

faqs.q: How many people live in Lake Oswego?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 39,722 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 40,731.

faqs.q: When are Clackamas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. The first date moves to the next business day when it falls on a weekend, as it did in 2025.
